newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian cen bank sees '97 growth below govt target.
newsitem.headline: Belgian cen bank sees '97 growth below govt target.

text.p: The National Bank of Belgium forecast the country's economy would grow by 2.0 percent in 1997, below a 2.1 percent target used by the government in drawing up its recent mini-budget.
The central bank also forecast inflation would average 1.9 percent.
According to the bank, Belgian gross domestic product (GDP) grew 1.4 percent in 1996, while inflation averaged 2.1 percent.
The forecasts were contained in the central bank's weekly "Economic Indicators for Belgium" publication and were the bank's first official statement on 1997.

Belgium's government reiterated last month its vital 1997 budget, which will be the yardstick for its bid for joining a single European currency, was based on a prudent growth forecast of 2.1 percent "while the average of recent forecasts is actually 2.2 percent."
Belgium aims to cut its deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997, below the 3.0 percent reference level set for European economic and monetary union membership.
The central bank gave no comment on its lower forecast.
